content.text:
The CLI supports per-message deletion through `slack api chat.delete`; it has no dedicated “clear DM” command.

- Use yyovil’s user token for yyovil’s messages and Clanker’s bot token for Clanker’s messages. Both need `chat:write`. [Slack documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.delete/)
- Enumerate thread replies before deletion. Deleting a parent leaves its replies, so delete replies first. [Slack documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/messaging/modifying-messages)
- `conversations.close` only closes the DM; it does not clear history. [Slack documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.close/)
- Verify every response has `ok: true`, then re-fetch fully paginated history and previously identified threads.

No messages were inspected or modified by this subagent.

content.text:
Built-in Slack CLI authentication cannot add `chat:write` to yyovil’s current credential.

- `auth login` has no scope option; `--token` only accepts an existing token.
- `auth token` uses the same authentication flow with rotation disabled. It does not request additional scopes. [CLI source](https://github.com/slackapi/slack-cli/blob/main/internal/api/auth.go)
- Deleting yyovil’s messages requires an existing authorized user token with `chat:write`, or OAuth authorization adding that user scope to an app. [Slack OAuth documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/tools/bolt-js/concepts/authenticating-oauth/)

Practical limitation: the available bot credential can delete Clanker’s messages, but the current CLI credential cannot delete yyovil’s messages. No authentication or permission changes were made.

Use the existing app’s settings flow if yyovil can access them:

1. Export Clanker’s manifest and add only `chat:write` under user scopes, preserving every existing field.
2. Reinstall to the workspace and approve as yyovil.
3. Retrieve the resulting **User OAuth Token** from OAuth & Permissions, verify its identity, then use it with Slack CLI deletion calls. [Official token instructions](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/using-web-api-with-postman/)

This avoids a callback server and client-secret handling. For a custom flow, Slack supports `user_scope=chat:write` followed by `oauth.v2.access`; the user token is returned under `authed_user`. [OAuth documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth/)

Avoid enabling PKCE on Clanker for this task: that change is irreversible without Slack support. [PKCE documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/using-pkce/)

Use an explicit credential, then verify `auth.test` returns the intended `team_id` and `user_id`; browser accounts do not choose CLI identity.

For a Slack permalink:

- Take channel ID from `/archives/<ID>/`.
- Prefer `thread_ts` query as the root timestamp. The `p…` path can identify a reply. [Slack permalink docs](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.getPermalink/)
- Call `conversations.replies channel=<ID> ts=<ROOT> limit=200`; follow `response_metadata.next_cursor` until empty. This includes parent and replies. [Thread API](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.replies/)

DM reads require `im:history`. Clanker’s bot token can read conversations it belongs to. [History permissions](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.history/)

No API calls, message reads, or changes performed.
